title: Breaking the Boundary Barrier: Robust Model Fingerprinting via Unlearnable Examples in Model-Parameter Space

problem.claim: Model ownership requires protection because deep learning models represent valuable intellectual property.

gap.claim: Existing decision-boundary fingerprints are fragile under fine-tuning, pruning, and adversarial training.

contributions.claim: MFUE fingerprints arbitrary modified models in parameter space using unlearnable examples.
Unlearnable examples can serve as stable fingerprints beyond model decision boundaries because of their persistent training resistance.
The method jointly optimizes unlearnable examples over models at different training stages using adversarial training to simulate model-modification randomness.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe MFUE as a novel fingerprinting methodology and identify their use of unlearnable examples as stable fingerprints beyond decision boundaries as the first such identification.

author_reported_evidence.claim: MFUE was evaluated against six attack types involving model and input tampering.
The authors report that MFUE outperforms four existing methods in robustness and uniqueness.

narrative_sequence.summary: Deep learning models are valuable intellectual property, motivating ownership protection.
Existing methods use adversarial examples to fingerprint decision boundaries, but those fingerprints are fragile under common model modifications.
MFUE uses the stable unlearnability of unlearnable examples for parameter-space fingerprinting and adds adversarial training across model stages for robustness.
The method is evaluated against six attack types, and the authors report improved robustness and uniqueness over four existing methods.

source_observation.claim: Decision-boundary fingerprints are sensitive to fine-tuning, pruning, and adversarial training, while unlearnable examples are presented as persistently resistant to training.

interpretation.claim: Fingerprinting signals tied to more stable model behavior may better survive model modifications than signals tied directly to decision boundaries.

application.claim: Model ownership systems could investigate parameter-space signals based on training resistance when robustness to model modification is important.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish robustness beyond the reported attack types or quantify how performance varies across modifications.

unknowns: No datasets, model architectures, or implementation details are specified.
No quantitative robustness or uniqueness results are provided.
The six attack types and four comparison methods are not identified.
No independent verification or reproducibility information is provided.
